extracted.intended_audience: card issuers, compliance officers, consumer-finance attorneys, and product teams administering credit card accounts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on compliance with Regulation Z (12 CFR part 1026) requirements governing due-date disclosures, limits on fees (including the 25% first-year limit), and permissible penalty/late fees and their calculation. Intended to help card issuers determine lawful fee practices and required disclosures for credit card accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of due date unaffected by state-law fee-assessment delays
rubrics_metrics.description: The due date disclosed under §1026.7(b)(11) is the contractual due date even if State law delays when a late fee may be assessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: issuer must disclose March 10 as due date per §1026.7(b)(11) but, under State law, may not assess a late fee before March 21.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure when fee or penalty rate is triggered by multiple events
rubrics_metrics.description: If a late payment fee or penalty rate is triggered only after multiple events (e.g., two late payments in six months), the issuer may but is not required to disclose the late payment and penalty rate each month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosures must be included on any periodic statement for which a late payment could trigger the fee or rate. Example: if a cardholder has one late payment, the disclosure must appear on each statement for the following five billing cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosing a range of late fees or penalty rates
rubrics_metrics.description: An issuer that imposes a range of late payment fees or rates may state the highest fee or rate and indicate lower fees or rates could be imposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible language: 'up to $8' as an example of indicating the maximum fee while allowing lower amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of penalty rate already in effect
rubrics_metrics.description: If the highest penalty rate has previously been triggered on an account, the issuer may delete the penalty-rate amount and the warning or may modify the language to indicate the penalty rate has been increased.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both deleting inapplicable warnings and modifying language to reflect an increased penalty rate are permitted but not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Same numerical day each month due-date requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The due date must generally be the same numerical date each month (e.g., the 25th of every month) to meet the 'same day each month' requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A due date that is the same relative date but not the same numerical date (e.g., third Tuesday) generally does not comply. Exception: the last day of each month may be used even though numerical date varies (e.g., Feb 28/29 and Aug 31).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted changes in due date
rubrics_metrics.description: A creditor may adjust a consumer's due date provided the new due date will be the same numerical date each month on an ongoing basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: honoring a consumer's request to change from the 20th to the 5th, or changing due date for operational reasons. See comment 2(a)(4)-3 for transitional billing-cycle guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Billing cycles longer than one month allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Billing cycles of two or three months are permitted provided the due date for each billing cycle is on the same numerical date of the month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: two-month cycles could show due dates January 25, March 25, May 25, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosing due date when creditor does not accept mail payments
rubrics_metrics.description: If the creditor does not accept or receive mailed payments on a day and must treat a mailed payment received the next business day as timely under §1026.10(d), the creditor must still disclose the contractual due date (the legal obligation) on the periodic statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: creditor must disclose July 4 as due date even if it treats a mailed payment received July 5 as timely under §1026.10(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: 25 percent limit on non-exempt fees during first year after account opening (§1026.52(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: During the first year after account opening, non-exempt fees charged to an account plus fees required to be paid by the consumer through other means may not exceed 25 percent of the credit limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to fees charged to the account and fees required through other means (e.g., payments from a consumer asset account). Numerous examples illustrate permissible and impermissible charges given credit limits and fee totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy when fees exceed 25 percent first-year limit
rubrics_metrics.description: If a fee charged exceeds the 25 percent limit, the issuer complies if it waives/removes the fee and any associated interest charges or credits the account for an amount equal to the fee and associated interest within a reasonable time but no later than the end of the billing cycle following the cycle during which the fee was charged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if a $2.50 fee pushed fees over the limit, issuer must waive/remove or credit $2.50 (plus related interest) by the end of the next billing cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of increases in credit limit during first year
rubrics_metrics.description: If the issuer increases the credit limit during the first year after account opening, §1026.52(a)(1) does not permit the issuer to require the consumer to pay additional fees that would otherwise be prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: increase from $400 to $600 does not allow charging additional fees based on the increase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of decreases in credit limit during first year
rubrics_metrics.description: If the issuer decreases the credit limit during the first year after account opening, the issuer must waive/remove or credit any fees that exceed 25 percent of the reduced limit within a reasonable time but no later than the end of the billing cycle following the cycle in which the limit was reduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if credit limit reduced from $1,000 to $600 and fees charged earlier exceeded 25% of $600, issuer must credit or remove the excess by the end of the next billing cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date on which account is considered open for first-year calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: For §1026.52(a)(1) purposes, an account is considered open no earlier than the date the account may first be used by the consumer to engage in transactions. An issuer may consider the account open on one of: the date of first use, the date the consumer complies with reasonable activation procedures (if usable that date), or seven days after mailing account-opening disclosures (with allowance to add issuer's reasonable mailing timeframe).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate treating account open on date of first transaction, on date consumer completes activation and may use account, or seven days after disclosures (plus additional days if issuer's reasonable mailing delay applies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'fee' for violating account terms (§1026.52(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of §1026.52(b), a fee includes any charge imposed by an issuer based on an act or omission that violates account terms or other requirements imposed by the issuer, excluding charges attributable to periodic interest rate increases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that APR increases resulting from violations are not treated as 'fees' under §1026.52(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of fees subject to §1026.52(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of fees subject to §1026.52(b) include late payment fees, returned payment fees, over-the-limit transaction fees (to the extent permitted), fees if payment on a check accessing the account is declined, fees for transactions the issuer declines to authorize, inactivity fees, and fees based on account closure/termination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References §1026.60(b)(9) and related commentary for late fees; some categories cross-reference other sections (e.g., §1026.56 for over-the-limit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of fees not subject to §1026.52(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees not covered by §1026.52(b) include balance transfer fees, cash advance fees, foreign transaction fees, annual fees and fees for issuance/availability of credit (except where based on inactivity), certain insurance or debt-cancellation fees, expedited payment fees, optional service fees, and reissuing a lost/stolen card.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1026.52(b)(2)(i)(B) and related commentary for specifics and exceptions (e.g., inactivity exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rounding fees to nearest whole dollar
rubrics_metrics.description: A card issuer may round any fee that complies with §1026.52(b) to the nearest whole dollar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a permitted $5.50 fee may be rounded up to $6. A permitted $5.49 fee may not be rounded up to $6, but may be rounded down to $5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application to hybrid prepaid-credit cards (covered separate credit features)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a covered separate credit feature and an asset feature on a prepaid account accessible by a hybrid prepaid-credit card, §1026.52(b) applies to any fee for violating the credit feature's terms regardless of whether that fee is imposed on the credit feature or on the asset feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a late fee tied to the credit feature is subject to §1026.52(b) even if charged on the asset feature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for fees on asset feature not part of the plan
rubrics_metrics.description: §1026.52(b) does not apply to fees or charges imposed on the asset feature of a prepaid account that are not charges imposed as part of the plan under §1026.6(b)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1026.6(b)(3)(iii)(D) and (E) and related commentary for treatment of non-plan charges on asset features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship of safe harbors and cost-based fees (§1026.52(b)(1)(i)/(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: An issuer may impose a fee for violations either by making a cost-based determination under §1026.52(b)(1)(i) or by complying with the safe harbors in §1026.52(b)(1)(ii). Complying with safe harbors does not require demonstrating fees represent a reasonable proportion of costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuer may use cost-based approach for some violation types and safe-harbor amounts for others. However, fees imposed under safe harbors still must not be inconsistent with prohibitions in §1026.52(b)(2). Examples explain permissible sequencing and limits (e.g., $25/$35 safe-harbor progression for returned-payment/over-the-limit fees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for cost-based penalty fees (§1026.52(b)(1)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: To use §1026.52(b)(1)(i) (fees based on costs), an issuer must have determined that a fee 'represents a reasonable proportion of the costs incurred ... as a result of that type of violation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant factors include: number of violations during a prior reasonable period (e.g., 12 months); costs incurred during that period due to those violations; optionally, number of fees imposed that issuer reasonably estimates it will be unable to collect; and optional reasonable estimates for upcoming period changes. See illustrative examples in comments 52(b)(1)(i)-6 through -9.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amounts excluded from cost analysis for cost-based fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain amounts are not costs for purposes of the cost-based determination: losses and associated costs (e.g., reserves, funding delinquent accounts, collection costs after charge-off) and costs associated with evaluating whether non-violating consumers are likely to violate (underwriting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, once a violation has occurred, costs associated with preventing additional violations for a reasonable period are costs incurred as a result of violations and may be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of third-party and affiliate charges in cost analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Amounts charged to the issuer by a third party as a result of a violation generally count as costs. If charged by an affiliate or subsidiary, the issuer must determine that the charge represents a reasonable proportion of the affiliate's/subsidiary's costs for that type of violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: affiliate collection services must reflect reasonable proportion of affiliate's costs incurred due to late payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparability to other issuers does not satisfy cost-based requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The fact that an issuer's fees are comparable to fees assessed by other issuers does not satisfy §1026.52(b)(1)(i)'s requirement that the fee represent a reasonable proportion of the issuer's costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuers must perform their own cost determinations rather than rely on market comparators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of uncollected fees in cost analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Issuers may consider fees they are unable to collect in determining appropriate fee amounts (e.g., fees on accounts charged off, fees discharged in bankruptcy, fees required to be waived to comply with law).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees the issuer voluntarily chooses not to impose or chooses not to collect (e.g., discretionary waivers to assist consumers) are not relevant to the cost determination. See illustrative examples in comments 52(b)(2)(i)-6 through -9.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs that may be included for late payment fee calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: For late payment fees, costs that may be considered include costs associated with the collection of late payments, notifying consumers of delinquencies, resolving delinquencies, and establishing workout and temporary hardship arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative numerical examples show how to compute a reasonable late fee based on past delinquencies, incurred costs, uncollected fees, and reasonable estimates of future changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs that may be included for returned-payment fees
rubrics_metrics.description: For returned-payment fees, costs include processing returned payments, reconciling systems/accounts, investigating potential fraud with respect to returned payments, and notifying the consumer and arranging for a new payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative examples show calculation of reasonable returned-payment fee amounts based on past returns, costs, and adjustments for uncollected fees or estimated future changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs that may be included and excluded for over-the-limit fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs included for over-the-limit fees: costs associated with determining whether to authorize over-the-limit transactions and costs of notifying the consumer and arranging payments to reduce the balance. Costs not included: costs associated with obtaining affirmative consent to pay transactions that exceed the credit limit (per §1026.56).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative examples provide computation of reasonable over-the-limit fees given numbers of transactions, costs incurred, limits on number of fees imposed due to affirmative consent rules, and adjustments for uncollected fees and forecasted changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs that may be included for declined access-check fees
rubrics_metrics.description: For declined access checks, costs include determining whether to decline payment, processing declined access checks and reconciling systems, investigating potential fraud, and notifying the consumer and merchant/other accepting party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An illustrative example: if issuer declined 100,000 access checks and incurred $2 million in related costs, the example guides how to derive a reasonable fee for future periods.
